synopsis: RadSimReal is a peer-reviewed radar sim-to-real study presented at CVPR 2024 [f327]. It provides on-road evidence that physical radar simulation can narrow the simulation-to-real gap for detection training, with the reported gap reduction limited to urban datasets [f3933, f472]. Nevertheless, the study shows a measurable domain gap, especially in adverse weather, so narrowing the gap does not mean eliminating it [f327, f472]. The glossary groups RadSimReal with Sim2Radar as research tools addressing the radar simulation-to-reality gap; the supplied evidence does not establish performance for heavy off-road machines [f15953, f3933, f472].

relations.note: Adds the urban-dataset limitation to the on-road gap-reduction finding.
Identifies a remaining measurable gap, especially in adverse weather, despite reported reduction.
